evidence.claim: Operator can dodge a DSS slashing by pre-scheduling an unstake and finalizing it (front-running requestSlashing) so the vault is no longer staked to the DSS, causing requestSlashing to revert with VaultNotStakedToDSS.
evidence.support_reason: requestSlashing validates isVaultStakeToDSS (SlasherLib.sol:51-52) and reverts if the vault was unstaked. finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS (Core.sol:146-153) is permissionless and only requires MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY (Operator.sol:93) plus matching root; the finish hook uses ignoreFailure:true (Operator.sol:128) and the request hook ignores failure for unstakes (Operator.sol:82), so a DSS cannot block finalization. Nothing in Core prevents the operator from finalizing the unstake before the DSS's requestSlashing lands.
preconditions: Operator has a vault staked to the DSS and has queued an unstake that has passed MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY
Operator can land finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS before the DSS's requestSlashing (ordering/front-run)
missing_evidence: The PoC's HostileHooksDSS reverts in requestUpdateStakeHook for unstakes, but the report's own text says the DSS can observe the request via that hook; a judge needs a PoC where the DSS behaves normally (non-reverting hooks) to show the evasion is not an artifact of a self-sabotaging DSS

The PoC uses a staker redeem of all shares in the same flow; need to show the slash is evaded even when the staker does not redeem (i.e., the vault remains funded but unstaked), to separate the unstake evasion from the withdrawal
No test showing the DSS could not have slashed earlier (e.g., that the slashing cooldown or veto window did not already give the DSS a chance), so the 'front-run' framing is not fully established
